documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit (pt in his truck on lunch break, consented to video).

Reviewed the 11/16 pulmonology consult with him: PFTs confirm COPD with incomplete reversibility; chronic bronchitis pattern; inhalers unchanged; pulmonology wants him off cigarettes. He understood the results as "my lungs are worse than I thought."
Breathing at his usual. Morning phlegm continues. No fever. Using both inhalers.
BP: no home cuff. HCTZ daily.
Still smoking a pack a day; says winter on the crew is the hardest time to cut down. Offered NRT patch plus lozenge; declines for now.

No exam beyond general appearance (comfortable, speaking full sentences, no audible wheeze on video).

A/P
- COPD, spirometry-confirmed as of 11/2020: continue fluticasone-salmeterol + albuterol PRN per pulmonology. Pulm f/u next fall.
- HTN: in-person BP check at physical.
- Tobacco use disorder: counseled; no quit date.
- COVID vaccine: eligible this spring for his age group/occupation, encouraged to book at the pharmacy when it opens up.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 54M.

Since last physical: pulmonology consult 11/2020 confirmed COPD on PFTs, chronic bronchitis picture. No chest infections since the spring 2020 pneumonia that he recalls. COVID vaccine series completed in April.
Today: no new complaints. Stairs still wind him; cough with morning sputum. No hemoptysis, chest pain, weight loss.
Tobacco 1 ppd, ~41 pack-years. Asked about readiness again: 3/10. Not setting a date.
Alcohol 1-2/month. Work same.
PHQ-2 0.

Meds reconciled: fluticasone-salmeterol 250/50 BID, albuterol PRN, HCTZ 25. NKDA.

Exam
BP 128/78 | HR 76 | SpO2 95% RA | Wt 79.2 kg | BMI 25.0
General: NAD.
Eyes/ENT: normal.
Neck: no adenopathy.
Resp: clear to auscultation, no wheeze.
CV: RRR, no murmur.
Abd: benign.
Ext: no edema, no clubbing or cyanosis.
Skin: nicotine staining R index and middle fingers.

Plan
- Fasting BMP and lipids drawn.
- COPD/HTN unchanged, continue meds.
- Tobacco: counseled.
- Flu shot in October; COVID booster when he becomes eligible.
- Pulm follow-up due November.

documents.title: Flu + COVID booster
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt here for flu vaccine and COVID booster; eligible as he has COPD and is past 6 months from his primary series. No reactions to prior doses except one day of arm soreness. Influenza quadrivalent IM L deltoid; Pfizer booster IM R deltoid. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 11/26/2021

Mr. Rossi returns one year after his initial evaluation for COPD. He has no complaints today and his breathing is at its baseline. What brought him in was worry about lung cancer: he still smokes and his father died of it.

Current medications: fluticasone propionate/salmeterol 250/50 BID, albuterol PRN, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Social: current smoker, one pack daily since age 13, approximately 42 pack-years.

Exam: BP 134/82, HR 77, SpO2 95% RA, weight 79.7 kg. His examination is unremarkable today.

Assessment:
1. COPD, stable.
2. High risk for lung cancer: age 55, about 42 pack-years, currently smoking. He meets criteria for annual low-dose CT screening.

Discussion: We talked through what screening with low-dose CT involves. I explained that many scans find small nodules that turn out to be benign, so a positive scan often leads to repeat imaging and occasionally a procedure, and that a negative scan does not remove all risk. We also discussed that the size at which a nodule is called positive is a choice: a lower size cut-off catches more cancers but labels more people with benign nodules as positive, and a higher one does the opposite. He asked good questions about what a positive result would mean for him, and after this conversation he would like to proceed. We also talked again about quitting, which would do more for his risk than any scan.

Plan:
- Low-dose CT lung cancer screening, annually. I would be grateful if your office would place the order so the results come to you.
- Continue current inhalers.
- Follow up in one year or sooner.

Pulmonology

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (baseline). Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast. Comparison: none. Lungs: emphysema. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation. Airways patent. Pleura: no effusion or pneumothorax. Mediastinum: no lymphadenopathy. Heart size normal. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Emphysema. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.

The device opens a little differently; the instruction sheet in the box shows how. If it feels like it is not working the same, call us.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL - 55 y/o male

Feels well. No interval illnesses or urgent care visits this year. Breathing unchanged from his baseline; morning cough. Using maintenance inhaler BID, rescue a few times a week. BP pill daily.
Smoker 1 ppd, ~43 pack-years. Declines a quit plan again.
Drinks rarely. Works demolition; currently on an older mill building teardown.
PHQ-2 0.

PMH: COPD (PFT-confirmed 2020), HTN, tobacco use disorder; in lung cancer screening (LDCT 12/2021 Lung-RADS 1).
Meds: fluticasone-salmeterol 250/50 BID; albuterol PRN; HCTZ 25 daily. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 137/80, HR 63, SpO2 95%, weight 80.4 kg, BMI 25.1.
Exam: Alert, NAD. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Lungs clear, no wheeze or crackles. CV regular, no murmurs. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Extremities without edema or clubbing. Skin: stained fingers. Neuro nonfocal.

Plan:
1. Labs: BMP, lipids, CBC today.
2. Pneumococcal: PCV20 today (COPD, smoker); no prior pneumococcal vaccine.
3. Lung cancer screening: annual LDCT ordered for December.
4. COPD, HTN: continue.
5. Tobacco: counseled, declines date/meds.
6. Flu and COVID updated booster in the fall.
7. Colonoscopy due 2027.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PROVIDER NOTE
Arrival 11/13/2022 13:05. Disposition 19:40, discharged.

CHIEF COMPLAINT: belly pain, constipation, irritable

HPI: 56-year-old man with COPD and current tobacco use with about six weeks of crampy abdominal pain that has been getting worse, along with constipation and feeling short-tempered. For roughly the past month people he works with have told him he has been irritable and is having a hard time staying on task with his work. He has not traveled and has not changed what he eats. No vomiting, no blood in the stool, no fever.

PMH: COPD, hypertension. Meds: fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, albuterol PRN, HCTZ 25 mg daily. NKDA.
Social: current smoker. Construction demolition worker.

EXAM: vitals as charted, afebrile.
General: no acute distress.
Abdomen: mild tenderness in the epigastrium, no rebound or guarding, bowel sounds present, no masses.
Neuro: speech is slowed and he is intermittently confused during the interview, but he is oriented to person, place and time. Moves all extremities.
Lungs: clear, no respiratory distress. Heart regular.

RESULTS:
Hgb 9.8, MCV 74. Iron 85, TIBC 360, transferrin saturation 24%, ferritin 110.
Hepatic enzymes and renal function within normal limits.
Peripheral smear (reviewed with lab): microcytic red cells with coarse basophilic stippling.
Abdominal radiograph, 2 views: nonobstructive bowel gas pattern; no free air.

MDM: Microcytic anemia with iron indices that do not suggest iron deficiency, coarse basophilic stippling on smear, abdominal colic, constipation and neurocognitive change in a demolition worker raise concern for lead toxicity. No obstruction on imaging; abdominal exam benign. Venous blood lead level sent; it is a send-out and will not result today. He is safe for discharge with close primary care follow-up; his PCP practice was messaged.

DISPOSITION: Discharged home. Follow up with PCP in 1-2 days for lead level result. Return for worsening pain, vomiting, confusion, weakness or seizure.

documents.title: ED discharge instructions
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body: You were seen for belly pain, constipation and feeling irritable and foggy. Your blood count is low and the blood smear raised concern for lead exposure from work. A blood lead level was sent and will come back in 1-3 days. Please call your primary care office Monday so they can see you this week. Do not return to work tasks that involve cutting, torching or sanding painted surfaces until you are cleared. Come back to the ED for vomiting, severe pain, worsening confusion, weakness or a seizure.

conditions.label: Lead poisoning
conditions.note: Occupational, demolition work; blood lead 62 µg/dL

documents.title: Lead level 62
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED sent the 11/13 visit summary yesterday. Blood lead from the ED resulted this morning: 62 µg/dL. With the stippled microcytic smear, belly pain, constipation and the irritability/concentration problems, this is lead poisoning, almost certainly occupational - he has been on a mill demolition cutting old painted steel.

Called pt. Explained the result. Still some cramping and constipation, less foggy than Sunday. No vomiting, no weakness, no headache. Lives alone. Told him not to go back to the cutting work. Seeing me tomorrow 2 pm. Discussed that I will need to file a report with the state and write him a work note.

documents.title: Post-ED visit, lead poisoning
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED visit.

ED 11/13: abdominal pain, constipation, irritability. Hgb 9.8, MCV 74, iron 85/TIBC 360/sat 24%/ferritin 110 (not iron deficient), smear with coarse basophilic stippling, KUB without obstruction. Venous blood lead 62 µg/dL resulted 11/15.

Today: cramping and constipation still there but milder. Coworkers had been on him about being short-tempered and losing track of tasks; he notices it less this week. No headache, no weakness in hands or feet, no vomiting.
Exposure: for about two months he has been torch-cutting and grinding painted structural steel on a mill demolition. Respirator only sometimes. Eats lunch on site. No hobbies with lead (no shooting, casting, stained glass). Lives alone, no kids at home.

BP 129/79, HR 66, SpO2 94%, wt 79.9 kg.
Alert and oriented, conversant, speech normal rate today, follows multistep commands. No gum line discoloration. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no rebound. Strength 5/5 grips and wrist extensors bilaterally. Lungs clear, no crackles.

A/P
1. Lead poisoning, occupational, BLL 62 µg/dL with anemia and GI/neurocognitive symptoms. Remove from exposure is the main treatment. Not pursuing chelation at this level with improving symptoms; will follow levels. Work note: no lead-exposed tasks until cleared. Reported to the state occupational lead surveillance program as required. Repeat blood lead and CBC in 4 weeks. Hygiene counseling: wash hands/face before eating or smoking, change clothes and boots before getting in the truck, wash work clothes separately.
2. Microcytic anemia - due to lead; recheck with BLL.
3. Tobacco use disorder - smoking with lead-dusted hands adds to the exposure; he says he will at least stop smoking on site. Still declines a quit date.
4. COPD, HTN - unchanged.
5. LDCT due 12/2022, already ordered.

documents.title: Work status note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:

Todd Rossi was seen in our office on 11/16/2022. For medical reasons he must not perform any lead-exposed tasks, including torch cutting, grinding, sanding, abrading or demolition of painted surfaces, until he is cleared by this office. He may perform other duties. We will update this restriction after his next blood test in about four weeks.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: State report - elevated blood lead
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mandatory report of adult elevated blood lead level submitted to the state occupational lead surveillance program.
Patient: Todd Rossi, DOB 10/02/1966. Venous BLL 62 µg/dL, collected 11/13/2022 (ED), resulted 11/15/2022.
Occupation: construction demolition laborer, commercial contractor. Suspected source: torch cutting of lead-painted structural steel.
Actions: removed from lead-exposed tasks; repeat BLL in 4 weeks.

documents.title: BLL 44
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called with results: blood lead down to 44 from 62; Hgb up to 11.4 from 9.8. He has been on site cleanup and debris hauling, no cutting, and wearing the respirator. Belly pain and constipation are easing; "maybe once a week now." Thinking feels clearer.
Plan: keep the restriction in place; repeat level and CBC in 2 months. Updated work note emailed to his supervisor at his request. LDCT is Monday.

reports.text: LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, ANNUAL LUNG CANCER SCREENING. Technique: low-dose helical CT without IV contrast. Comparison: 12/20/2021. Lungs: emphysema, similar to prior. No pulmonary nodule. No consolidation or mass. Central airways patent. No pleural effusion. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Heart normal in size. Upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Emphysema, unchanged. Continue annual screening in 12 months.
